ATP effect hypotheses — low-ATP fit and the 8 vs 2 mM head-to-head

Two questions, one parameter set. The ATP gates are exactly 1 at MgATP_ref, so both conditions below come from a single parameter file and differ only by [MgATP] — the 8 mM and 2 mM curves are not two fits.

Baseline: the same parametrisation as the H0–H4 hypothesis ladder (params/lowATP_H2_chem_opt.m = the ladder's core + the H2, seven-gate, chemically-defensible set). See §4 for a caveat about that core.

1. Headline

The model reproduces the ATP effect within between-preparation scatter for 10 of 12 scored features. Only vall2_dy and rsK genuinely fail.

That is a stronger and better-grounded verdict than every previous report in this project, because it judges the model against the spread of what the data is (three 2026 protocol days) rather than against the single preparation it was fitted to.

2. The ATP effect itself

Ratios are formed per preparation and then averaged, so the SD is the real between-prep spread of the effect, not of the levels.

feature data 2/8 ±SD model inside ±1 SD?
steady 1.376 0.246 1.160 yes
A 0.993 0.057 1.025 yes
peak1_y 1.039 0.177 1.059 yes
vall_y 1.027 0.102 0.927 yes
peak2 1.011 0.107 0.909 yes
vall2_dy 0.970 0.178 1.464 no
ktr 0.540 0.051 0.506 yes
rsK 0.345 0.061 0.627 no
restretchSlopeStart 1.265 0.310 1.085 yes
peak1_dSL 1.293 0.568 1.219 yes
vall_t 0.950 0.552 1.113 yes
rsR2 1.187 0.101 1.001 no — but see below

Three things worth reading off this:

  • ktr is essentially exact (0.506 vs 0.540 ± 0.051). The isometric redevelopment slowdown at low ATP is a solved problem.
  • Most features show no ATP effect at all once each preparation is scaled by its own steady force — A, peak1_y, vall_y, peak2, vall2_dy all sit at 1.0 ± 0.1 in the data. The 2 mM phenotype is **a force scale-up plus two rate slowdowns**, not a change of waveform shape. The model gets that structure right.
  • rsR2 is a non-defect. The model produces a noise-free single exponential, so the restretch-recovery R² pins at exactly 1.000 while real traces sit at 0.87. It is bounded 0.4–1.0 in the objective and scores zero either way.

Absolute force: 2 mM 84.7 ± 6.1 kPa vs 8 mM 63.3 ± 14.8 kPa, ratio ×1.34 — consistent with ATPEffectReconciliation's rundown-corrected ×1.36. The 8 mM spread is 3× wider (CV 23 % vs 7 %), which is why steady carries the loosest error bar despite being the largest effect.

3. Force-velocity and power, both conditions

The model separates the two conditions in the right direction and by about the right amount. Two residuals:

  • 8 mM mid-velocity concavity — the known error: model is +6 % at 0.5 ML/s and −20 % at 2 ML/s. Pinned correctly at both ends.
  • 2 mM power peak position. Data peak power is at **v = 1.0 ML/s at both concentrations; the model puts the 2 mM peak at 0.5**. The model predicts a leftward shift with low ATP that the data do not show. (An earlier report of mine offered that shift as a falsifiable prediction and claimed the data did not exist. It did — Data_ATP column 4 — and it falsifies the prediction.)

4. The low-ATP fit against the 3-preparation envelope

Every trace and every force-dimension feature is divided by its own mean steady before averaging, because absolute force is not transferable between preparations. The band is therefore the spread of the shape. 03/27 — the fit target — is drawn separately in every panel: a deviation from the 3-prep mean is only a defect if it is also a deviation from 03/27.

Model steady 88.8 kPa against data 84.7 ± 6.1 — inside 1 SD. The model tracks 03/27 almost exactly through cycles 1–3. The systematic error is confined to two places: the re-stretch spike overshoots (model 1.35 vs data 1.18 at cycle 1, in every cycle), and cycles 4–5 sit above the band — though 03/27 itself is at the top of the band there, so part of that is the fit target being the strongest preparation.

valley −0.3 rsR2 +5.5 (the R²=1 artifact)
peak2 −0.5 vall2_dy −3.9

There is no 2 mM staircase dataset — only protocol_*_velocitytable_stairs.mat at 8 mM. That panel is therefore the 2 mM model as an unconstrained prediction against the 8 mM trace, and the cost of 0.035 is against 8 mM data. It is shown for completeness, not as evidence. The model's step-transients overshoot the 8 mM measurement substantially; whether that is an ATP effect or a model defect cannot be told without a 2 mM staircase.

5. Caveat on the baseline

This report keeps the H0–H4 parametrisation, as requested, so it is directly comparable with the hypothesis ladder. But that core is joint82_opt, whose 8 mM cost is 4.0094 against realign4_opt's 3.8513 — the joint refit traded 8 mM away to buy 2 mM, and the ladder was then seeded from the traded-away core.

  • The ladder's ranking is unaffected: every rung shared this core.
  • The absolute costs are inflated by roughly that 0.16 at 8 mM plus whatever the distortion costs at 2 mM.
  • The production H1/H2/H3 runs should start from realign4_opt, with the core snapshot as an explicit top-of-file parameter rather than buried in a loadParams call — which is how this slipped past unnoticed.

6. Where the residual actually is

Stripping out the non-defects (rsR2) and the features that are within between-preparation scatter, the low-ATP model has exactly three problems, and two of them are the same problem:

  1. rsK — post-restretch recovery, ×1.8 too fast as a ratio and +10.4 SD in absolute terms. Note this is the residual of a defect already seriously attacked in RestretchSRXRecoil (load realignment took it ×2.35 → ×1.12); the present core partially undid that.
  2. The re-stretch spike overshoots in every cycle, which is vall2_dy (−3.9 SD) and peak1_dSL (+2.4 SD) in feature terms. Same window as (1).
  3. vall_t (+6.1 SD) — model 12–18 ms vs data 3–8 ms. A sub-10 ms timing error, low-weighted, but real.

Everything in the low-ATP phenotype outside the re-stretch window is reproduced within the spread of the data.

Drivers: RunLowAtpFitReport.m, RunAtpHeadToHead.m. Both are standalone and can be run in parallel. Results in results/.
